notes:
A module update can now happen in two steps: upd_fetch_files() downloads the files into a temporary folder, the slow part (about 100 s for the 300 files of AUTH), and upd_apply_files() puts them in place, about two seconds. A nightly maintenance can thus keep the site open while it downloads and close it only for the second step. Each file is written beside its target and renamed over it, so a page never reads half a file, and version.json goes last, so an interrupted run keeps the former version number and is simply played again. upd_sync_files() is built on the two and keeps its contract: what arrived is written, the rest is reported.

A missing file is no longer written as its error page. The downloads keep the body of an HTTP error to report GitHub's reason, and raw.githubusercontent.com answers a missing file with the text "404: Not Found", which was written in place of the file; the status of the response now decides. Manifest paths that would leave the module folder ("..", a leading slash) are refused for modules as they already were for _shared.

Previously (1.3.5): A module can now announce its new versions on the ianseo home page, the way the core already reminds the administrator to check its own updates: one line under the title naming the module, the version waiting in the repository and a link to the module's update screen. Only the administrator sees it — with an account module, the server administrator view only.

It never slows a page down. The menu reads one row of the core Parameters table and nothing else; when that cached answer is too old, the browser asks the new notice.php once the page has finished loading, in a single request for every module concerned, and that endpoint releases the session lock before going on the network. It reads only the version number: an HTTP Range asks for the first 128 bytes of version.json (19 KB for AUTH with its release notes). A successful answer is kept 12 hours for the whole installation, a failed one an hour; without an Internet connection the notice stays silent.

On by default, it is switched off from the module's update screen (new block "Notice on the home page"). Checking for updates on that screen also refreshes the notice, so the two never disagree. A module opts in with two guarded lines in its menu.php and 'notice' => true on its update screen; notice-lib.php explains how. No table of its own: two rows of Parameters, UpdNoticeOff and UpdNoticeCache.

Previously (1.3.4): The update and uninstall screens use the whole width of the page instead of a fixed column.

Previously (1.3.3): Shared machinery brought up to the standard asked of published modules.

The update and uninstall screens are translated once for every module, in English, French, Italian, German and Spanish, through upd_text() and languages/ — a module no longer carries its own copy of that wording.

paths.php discovers the ianseo root and a module's URL instead of counting directory levels, so a module keeps working wherever it is installed. schema-lib.php offers existence tests that cannot be fatal, non-fatal column additions, and idempotent table and column renames that leave a compatibility view under the old name; uninstalling now removes those views too.

Both screens are written in PHP rather than woven out of template tags, which is what ianseo asks: a file should be in one language at a time. Every value passes through one short escaping helper. One display bug fell out of that rewrite — the uninstall page listed a module's tables by joining them with markup and then escaping the whole string, so the reader saw the tags as text between each table name.

Code and comments in English. upd_current_user() cut the user name with substr(), which counts bytes and can split a character in half; it uses mb_substr() now.
